title: Throughput regression — continuous batching (scratchpad 24)
content:
Background:
- Regression noticed after rolling quantization+kernel update (PR 439) on 2026-02-20.
- Production serving pools (pool-gpu-small) saw ~25-40% drop in overall tokens/s for short chat workloads (avg prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Issue only under continuous batching enabled workloads; single-request latency unaffected.

Initial signals:
- Alerts: throughput-degraded-high triggered by synthetic-slo alert (token_throughput < 75% baseline for 10m).
- Grafana: per-shard tokens/s drop. P95 latency stable; P99 spiky when autoscaling happens.
- Prom query (rough):
  - rate(tokens_processed_total{pool="pool-gpu-small"}[5m]) dropped from ~8500/s -> ~5200/s between 2026-02-20T02:15 and 02:40 UTC.
  - batch_size_avg increased from 3.1 -> 6.9 in same window (unexpected).

Repro (local synthetic):
1) Start local runner (gpu-profile small)
   ./scripts/run_local_inference.sh --model redwood-v1 --pool pool-gpu-small --workers 8
2) Synthetic load generator (keeps open sessions, continuous batching on):
   python tools/loadgen.py --qps 80 --session-length 120 --continuous-batching --kv-cache true
3) Observe: tokens/s lower than pre-change baseline.

Commands tried (notes + output snippets):
- Inspect active batching config on node:
  curl -s http://node-4:8080/debug/batching_config | jq .
  => "continuous_batching: enabled", "max_pending_requests: 200", "batch_timeout_ms: 10"

- Dump runtime flags from process:
  ps aux | grep inference_runtime | grep -v grep
  => /opt/bin/inference_runtime --enable-continuous-batching=true --max-batch-warmup=0 --kv-cache-mode=dynamic

- Live tail logs for a degraded timeframe:
  2026-02-20T02:22:11.215Z INFO batcher.cpp:324 BatchFlushed size=13 latency_ms=27 kv_cache_miss=0.62
  2026-02-20T02:22:11.216Z WARN runtime.cpp:90 KernelFallback: selected kernel "matmul_v2" slower than baseline by 1.8x
  2026-02-20T02:22:12.003Z INFO scheduler.cpp:210 QueuedRequests=180 batch_in_flight=4
  2026-02-20T02:22:12.007Z ERROR worker.cpp:412 failed to apply kv-cache prefix merge: inconsistent-kv-length (retryable)

- Quick profiling snapshot (perf-like):
  top functions: attention_kernel (40%), matmul_v2 (18%), kv_merge (12%), memcpy (9%), scheduler (5%)

Hypotheses so far:
- H1: Kernel selection change (PR 439) regresses matmul throughput for short sequences and causes larger batch sizes to be selected by scheduler to compensate, net throughput down.
- H2: KV cache merge bug increases per-request overhead under continuous batching (seen error consistent with kv merge failure), causing longer processing per batch and more queueing -> larger batch sizes but lower tokens/s.
- H3: Batching timeout interplay: batch_timeout_ms set to 10ms combined with max_pending_requests increased allows big batches of short requests that are not vectorized well by new kernels.

Quick experiments executed:
- Roll back kernel selection override (on a single canary node):
  kubectl set env deploy/serving-runtime node-4 KERNEL_OVERRIDE="kernel_v1"
  -> tokens/s on node-4 recovered to ~92% baseline within 4m.
  -> suggests kernel selection is a major contributor.

- Toggle continuous batching off on a canary pool:
  curl -X POST http://orchestrator.local/api/pools/pool-gpu-small/config -d '{"continuous_batching":false}'
  -> tokens/s for that pool increases to baseline, but overall tail latency for single requests increases (expected).

- Force KV-cache strict mode (disable dynamic merges):
  set via configmap: kv_cache.mode = "strict" (no merges)
  -> saw fewer kv merge errors in logs; tokens/s marginally improved (~5%), but still below baseline.

Notes about reproducer reliability:
- Reproducer depends on keeping sessions warm (kv-cache hits). If sessions cold, behavior differs (smaller batch sizes, more overhead).
- Problem seems amplified for short-sequence chat workloads with many small messages per session (typical product traffic).

Actionable next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Run A/B on kernel selection: fully revert PR 439 on a 10% traffic pool for 6h and collect p95/p99 tokens/s and kernel perf counters.
- [ ] Add additional metrics: per-kernel flops/s, avg sequence length histogram, per-batch kv_merge_time_ms. (prom exporter update)
- [ ] Add assertion in batcher: if average batch_size > 5 for sequences < 200 tokens, emit metric and optionally reduce batch_timeout_ms.
- [ ] Root-cause kv-merge error: instrument failing code path to dump request ids and kv sizes on inconsistent-kv-length. File issue in repo (JIRA-INF-847).
- [ ] Prepare rollback plan for PR 439 (already drafted in github PR 439 commentary).

Notes to self (observations / heuristics):
- Kernel fallback logs often coincide with spikes in batch_size_avg. If a kernel fallback is slower, scheduler backlogs and batch sizes grow trying to amortize overhead -> paradoxically lowers tokens/s.
- Continuous batching masks per-request overhead but also couples multiple code paths (kv merge, kernel selection). Need better isolation in testing harness to exercise continuous-batching + kv-cache simultaneously.

Short-term mitigation options considered:
- Temporarily reduce max_pending_requests to 40 on pool-gpu-small to cap batch-size growth.
- Reduce batch_timeout_ms to 3ms to encourage smaller batches for short sequences. Risk: more context-switches and slightly higher per-token latency for larger sequences.
- Disable kernel_v2 selection for sequence length < 256 (heuristic) until we can benchmark.

Last run notes (2026-02-25 09:20 UTC):
- Applied kernel revert on canary and toggled kv-cache strict on 2 nodes. Aggregate tokens/s improved to ~88% baseline; p99 latency still noisy. Collecting more traces.

References / links:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/439
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-847 (kv-merge inconsistency)
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-1123 (postmortem-in-progress)

If stuck, ping Arjun or Lina in #eng-serving-runtime; Lina has the perf rig for reproducing short-seq workloads.

-- Maya
